result.markdown: --- title: "Hessian and Likelihood" description: "A discussion on confidence intervals" author: "Zhenglei Gao" date: "11/20/2024" categories: - code - Stats - R editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- When discussing with Johannes, I mentioned that GoF is making sense when comparing with other models, most of the time with Null or full models. ## General considerations When used in nonlinear regression, the pseudo $R^2$ cannot be interpreted as in linear regression. ## Try with some examples From the pscl package: - llh: The log-likelihood from the fitted model - llhNull: The log-likelihood from the intercept-only restricted model - G2: Minus two times the difference in the log-likelihoods - McFadden: McFadden's pseudo r-squared - r2ML: Maximum likelihood pseudo r-squared - r2CU: Cragg and Uhler's pseudo r-squared ### Example with random data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Load necessary libraries library(MASS) ## install.packages("pscl") library(pscl) # For the pseudo R-squared function ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: package 'pscl' was built under R version 4.4.2 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Classes and Methods for R originally developed in the Political Science Computational Laboratory Department of Political Science Stanford University (2002-2015), by and under the direction of Simon Jackman. hurdle and zeroinfl functions by Achim Zeileis. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Simulate some data set.seed(123) n <- 100 x <- rnorm(n) y <- rbinom(n, 1, prob = 0.5) # Random binary outcome that is not related to x # Fit a logistic regression model model <- glm(y ~ x, family = binomial) # Calculate pseudo R-squared pseudo_r2 <- pR2(model) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` fitting null model for pseudo-r2 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} print(pseudo_r2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` llh llhNull G2 McFadden r2ML -68.920601482 -69.234696709 0.628190454 0.004536674 0.006262215 r2CU 0.008354080 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} summary(lm(y~predict(model))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = y ~ predict(model)) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -0.5428 -0.4866 -0.3965 0.5260 0.5735 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 0.49998 0.05637 8.870 3.42e-14 *** predict(model) 0.24817 0.31575 0.786 0.434 --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 0.5031 on 98 degrees of freedom Multiple R-squared: 0.006264, Adjusted R-squared: -0.003876 F-statistic: 0.6177 on 1 and 98 DF, p-value: 0.4338 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Check the model summary summary(model) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: glm(formula = y ~ x, family = binomial) Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|) (Intercept) -0.09639 0.20191 -0.477 0.633 x 0.17543 0.22231 0.789 0.430 (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1) Null deviance: 138.47 on 99 degrees of freedom Residual deviance: 137.84 on 98 degrees of freedom AIC: 141.84 Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Visualize the fit plot(x, y, main = "Logistic Regression Fit", xlab = "x", ylab = "y") points(x, fitted(model), col = "red", pch = 19) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](PseudoR2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### Example where R2 works ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Simulate data with outliers # Load necessary libraries library(MASS) library(pscl) # For the pseudo R-squared function # Simulate some data set.seed(456) n <- 100 x <- rnorm(n) x0 <- x # Create a binary outcome based on a logistic function y <- rbinom(n, 1, prob = plogis(x)) y0 <- y # Introduce influential points by adding extreme values to the predictor r1 <- order(x) ind <- r1[91:100] ind <- r1[1:10] x[ind] <- rep(3, 10) # Make these points influential by shifting x # Recalculate the binary response based on the new x values y[ind] <- rbinom(10, 1, prob = plogis(x[ind])) # Ensure y is binary # Fit a logistic regression model model_with_influential_points <- glm(y ~ x0, family = binomial) summary(lm(y~predict(model_with_influential_points))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = y ~ predict(model_with_influential_points)) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -0.6966 -0.5061 0.3009 0.4337 0.6795 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 0.49994 0.05396 9.265 4.77e-15 *** predict(model_with_influential_points) 0.24128 0.12965 1.861 0.0657 . --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 0.4948 on 98 degrees of freedom Multiple R-squared: 0.03413, Adjusted R-squared: 0.02428 F-statistic: 3.463 on 1 and 98 DF, p-value: 0.06574 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} model_without_influential_points <- glm(y ~ x, family = binomial) summary(lm(y0~predict(model_without_influential_points))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = y0 ~ predict(model_without_influential_points)) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -0.6667 -0.4104 -0.3316 0.5131 0.6904 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 0.43755 0.05067 8.635 1.1e-13 predict(model_without_influential_points) 0.05975 0.03029 1.973 0.0513 (Intercept) *** predict(model_without_influential_points) . --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 0.4937 on 98 degrees of freedom Multiple R-squared: 0.03819, Adjusted R-squared: 0.02838 F-statistic: 3.892 on 1 and 98 DF, p-value: 0.05135 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Calculate pseudo R-squared pseudo_r2_outliers <- pR2(model_with_influential_points) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` fitting null model for pseudo-r2 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} print(pseudo_r2_outliers) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` llh llhNull G2 McFadden r2ML r2CU -67.26284391 -68.99437585 3.46306388 0.02509671 0.03403786 0.04548126 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} rbind(pseudo_r2_outliers,pR2(model_without_influential_points)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` fitting null model for pseudo-r2 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` llh llhNull G2 McFadden r2ML pseudo_r2_outliers -67.26284 -68.99438 3.463064 0.02509671 0.03403786 -51.49928 -68.99438 34.990197 0.25357282 0.29524283 r2CU pseudo_r2_outliers 0.04548126 0.39450231 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Check the model summary summary(model_with_influential_points) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: glm(formula = y ~ x0, family = binomial) Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|) (Intercept) 0.1199 0.2051 0.585 0.5588 x0 0.3830 0.2103 1.821 0.0686 . --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1) Null deviance: 137.99 on 99 degrees of freedom Residual deviance: 134.53 on 98 degrees of freedom AIC: 138.53 Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Predict probabilities predicted_probabilities <- predict(model_with_influential_points, type = "response") # Classify predictions (using 0.5 as the cutoff) predicted_classes <- ifelse(predicted_probabilities > 0.5, 1, 0) # Calculate classification error classification_error <- mean(predicted_classes != y) print(paste("Classification Error:", round(classification_error, 4))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Classification Error: 0.42" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Predict probabilities predicted_probabilities <- predict(model_without_influential_points, type = "response") # Classify predictions (using 0.5 as the cutoff) predicted_classes <- ifelse(predicted_probabilities > 0.5, 1, 0) # Calculate classification error classification_error <- mean(predicted_classes != y0) print(paste("Classification Error:", round(classification_error, 4))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Classification Error: 0.3" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Visualize the fit plot(x0, y, main = "Logistic Regression Fit with Influential Points", xlab = "x", ylab = "y", ylim = c(-0.1, 1.1)) points(x0, fitted(model_with_influential_points), col = "green", pch = 3) points(x0[ind], y0[ind]-0.1, col = "red", pch = 3) points(x0[ind], y[ind]-0.05, col = "darkgreen", pch = 4) points(x0, fitted(model_without_influential_points), col = "red", pch = 19) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](PseudoR2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## A case where R^2 can be 0 to 1 depending on x is between (-3,3), (-3,6), (-1,3)! ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Create data that does not fit a logistic model well set.seed(789) n <- 100 x <- seq(-3, 6, length.out = n) y <- ifelse(x^2 > 1, 1, 0) # Nonlinear relationship y1 <- ifelse(x > 0, 1, 0) # Perfect fit # Fit a logistic regression model model_nonlinear <- glm(y ~ x, family = binomial) # Calculate pseudo R-squared pseudo_r2_nonlinear <- pR2(model_nonlinear) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` fitting null model for pseudo-r2 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} print(pseudo_r2_nonlinear) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` llh llhNull G2 McFadden r2ML r2CU -48.80265582 -53.92763415 10.24995667 0.09503436 0.09742146 0.14762782 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} xa <- rep(1,length(y)) summary(lm(y~predict(model_nonlinear))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = y ~ predict(model_nonlinear)) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -0.74495 0.01252 0.12525 0.23797 0.45545 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 0.54857 0.07910 6.935 4.38e-10 *** predict(model_nonlinear) 0.16011 0.04918 3.256 0.00155 ** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 0.4038 on 98 degrees of freedom Multiple R-squared: 0.0976, Adjusted R-squared: 0.08839 F-statistic: 10.6 on 1 and 98 DF, p-value: 0.001554 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Check the model summary summary(model_nonlinear) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: glm(formula = y ~ x, family = binomial) Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|) (Intercept) 0.9136 0.2547 3.588 0.000334 *** x 0.3129 0.1054 2.969 0.002991 ** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1) Null deviance: 107.855 on 99 degrees of freedom Residual deviance: 97.605 on 98 degrees of freedom AIC: 101.61 Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Visualize the fit plot(x, y, main = "Logistic Regression Fit for Nonlinear Data", xlab = "x", ylab = "y") points(x, fitted(model_nonlinear), col = "red", pch = 19) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](PseudoR2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Some Additional Notes - https://rcompanion.org/rcompanion/b_04.html ## G-test = Likelihood ratio test? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} observed = c(1752, 1895) # observed frequencies expected = c(0.5, 0.5) # expected proportions library(DescTools) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: package 'DescTools' was built under R version 4.4.2 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} GTest(x=observed, p=expected, correct="none") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Log likelihood ratio (G-test) goodness of fit test data: observed G = 5.6085, X-squared df = 1, p-value = 0.01787 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} degrees = 1 # degrees of freedom observed = c(1752, 1895) # observed frequencies expected.prop = c(0.5, 0.5) # expected proportions expected.count = sum(observed)*expected.prop G = 2 * sum(observed * log(observed / expected.count)) pchisq(G, df=degrees, lower.tail=FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.01787343 ``` ::: ::: ### $R^2$ can only increase when adding more variables ::: {.cell} ::: ## An error in reporting R2. The null mean model is different in those two types of model specifications, even though they are the same model. ::: callout-note r.squared: R^2, the ‘fraction of variance explained by the model’, R^2 = 1 - Sum(R[i]^2) / Sum((y[i]- y*)^2), where y* is the mean of y[i] if there is an intercept and zero otherwise. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library("sigr") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: package 'sigr' was built under R version 4.4.2 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} library("broom") set.seed(23255) d <- data.frame(y= runif(100), x= ifelse(runif(100)>=0.5, 'a', 'b'), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) m1 <- lm(y~x, data=d) t(broom::glance(m1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] r.squared 0.002177326 adj.r.squared -0.008004538 sigma 0.302851476 statistic 0.213843593 p.value 0.644796456 df 1.000000000 logLik -21.432440763 AIC 48.864881526 BIC 56.680392084 deviance 8.988463618 df.residual 98.000000000 nobs 100.000000000 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} d$pred1 <- predict(m1, newdata = d) cat(render(sigr::wrapFTest(d, 'pred1', 'y'), format='markdown')) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` **F Test** summary: (R^2^=0.002177, *F*(1,98)=0.2138, *p*=n.s.). ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} m2 <- lm(y~0+x, data=d) t(broom::glance(m2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] r.squared 7.524811e-01 adj.r.squared 7.474297e-01 sigma 3.028515e-01 statistic 1.489647e+02 p.value 1.935559e-30 df 2.000000e+00 logLik -2.143244e+01 AIC 4.886488e+01 BIC 5.668039e+01 deviance 8.988464e+00 df.residual 9.800000e+01 nobs 1.000000e+02 ``` ::: :::
